source.title: Disentangling Neuron Representations with Concept Vectors
source.authors: Laura O'Mahony; V. Andrearczyk; H. Muller; Mara Graziani

record.file_problem: The paper, appendix and references are present; the extracted text has some PDF layout/column artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses neuron polysemanticity and reports results for a concept-vector method on Inception V3, but it does not test any of the specified claim versions: it does not audit neuron-pole job shares, the named InceptionV1 example, attribution graphs, or explanation scoring on held-out activations.
record.gate_note: The paper's results concern clustering image activations and evaluating the resulting concept vectors. They do not measure any of the quantities or tests named in V1–V7. Reported findings are recorded with versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The study proposes a clustering method that splits Inception V3 neurons into concept vectors. It does not measure any quantity named in V1–V7: no LLM neuron-pole job shares, no cross-model or scale audit, and no InceptionV1 cat-and-car reanalysis. It also has no tool or architecture comparison of interpretable shares, no attribution graphs, and no held-out activation-prediction scoring of explanations. Its one share-like statement (r8, a majority of analysed Mixed 7b neurons show some polysemanticity) gives no count or proportion. It also does not test what causes polysemanticity, so it cannot bear on V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that polysemantic neurons can be disentangled into concept vectors (linear combinations of neurons) that encode coherent, human-understandable features. They find these vectors align with the relevant activations better than neuron directions, and that exploring directions rather than neurons may yield better fundamental units. Stated limitations are reliance on the clustering data and use of image data only.
record.recipe_differences: This is an image-model concept-discovery and clustering method, not an audit of neuron-pole job shares or held-out neuron-explanation scoring.
record.method_sensitivity: The number and granularity of concepts depend on the distance threshold; the paper reports different cluster counts for neuron 1 at different thresholds.

fits_no_version.finding: In Inception V3 Mixed 7b, the majority of analysed neurons show some polysemanticity by inspection of top-100 activating images (count not given). Example neurons: 35 (apples/sports), 5 (peacocks/vans) and 27 (toilet paper/dog faces) are polysemantic; 16 (elliptical shapes) and 13 (dark backgrounds) are monosemantic. Neuron 1 (underwater/scuba) splits into related facets depending on the threshold.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Late-layer neurons of a standard ImageNet CNN (Inception V3) often respond to several distinct image groups when inspected via top activating examples, and the number of groups depends on the clustering threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Concept vectors derived from clusters were judged coherent by human raters: 100% intruder accuracy and 97% label agreement (n=8). They also align with cluster activations better than the neuron direction does.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Directions in activation space found by clustering a neuron's top activating examples give more coherent units than the neuron itself for polysemantic vision neurons.

record.peer_reviewed: 2023 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
record.problems: Exploratory proof-of-concept using an undersampled ImageNet dataset with 130 random images per class; only image data were studied. The paper states that results rely on the data used to generate clusters. The number of neurons analysed is not stated, and some reported comparisons are qualitative rather than numerical.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B or any LLM neuron-pole audit, and no job-share proportions.
No language models, no dense versus mixture-of-experts comparison, no scale range.
Does not examine InceptionV1's cat-and-car neuron or any shared-feature reinterpretation. The neuron 35 apples/sports split is not tested for a shared underlying feature.

No comparison of architectures, regularization or tools, and no quantified interpretable share. The statement that most analysed Mixed 7b neurons show some polysemanticity has no count and no causal test.
No attribution graphs or circuit-level explanation of behaviour.
No test of whether explanations predict activations beyond the top activating examples.
No simulation-based automated scoring of explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The study frames neurons as often polysemantic and cites superposition, a stance opposite to the essay. However, its evidence is qualitative and unquantified (r8 gives no count), uses an undersampled ImageNet, and covers a single layer of Inception V3, not InceptionV1. It is therefore context, not a test of any version. The reader's relation and tranche are accepted.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or their job-share proportions.
No comparison across language models, dense or mixture-of-experts architectures, or model scales.
Does not examine the InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron or test the proposed shared-pose interpretation.
Does not estimate the share of interpretable neurons or compare architectures, regularization, or tool quality as causes of that share.
No attribution graphs or test of whether model behaviour can be explained by the model's neurons without a replacement model.
Does not test explanations against activations beyond those used to form them or measure false predictions about where neurons fire.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

relation.reason: Discusses polysemantic neurons and superposition but does not test or use the claim.

tranche.reason: Concept-vector clustering method on Inception V3. Nothing is measured on LLM neuron-pole shares, the InceptionV1 cat-car reanalysis, or tool/architecture effects, so it tests no version.

source_check.notes: All 11 rows match the text. The study lists no verdicts or statements. The row closest to the claim is r8: 'the majority' of the Mixed 7b neurons analysed showed some polysemanticity, judged from top-activating images. It gives no count and has no link to a version. The text gives no numbers for the Fig. 5 comparison (r11). Figure labels in the paper are inconsistent: Fig. 2's caption lists only (a) and (b), and the body text calls neuron 27's panel A.7c where the caption says A.7d.
